log.thought: Thought: Starting with a standard balanced baseline: moderate depth 4, learning rate 0.05, 200 trees, moderate regularization.
Thought: Testing shallower depth 3 with higher regularization and lower learning rate to see if simpler trees generalize better on imbalanced data.

Thought: Testing depth 6 with moderate subsampling and slightly higher learning rate (0.04), n_estimators 180, min_child_weight 3, to check if higher interaction depth captures complex overtake dynamics.
Thought: Checking depth 4 with lower min_child_weight (1) and lower learning rate (0.03) to see if finer leaf splits help identify subtle minority patterns.
Thought: Trial 4 improved with lower min_child_weight. Testing depth 5 with min_child_weight 1 and similar regularization/subsampling to check if slightly deeper trees improve performance.
Thought: Depth 5 with min_child_weight 1 gave 0.5574. Testing min_child_weight 2 at depth 5 to see if slight regularization against leaf variance helps.
Thought: min_child_weight 2 bumped PR-AUC to 0.5610. Testing min_child_weight 3 with the exact same other settings to map the sensitivity to min_child_weight.
Thought: min_child_weight=2 was best for depth 5. Testing depth 6 with min_child_weight=2 and otherwise identical settings to trial 6.
Thought: Testing depth 4 with min_child_weight 2 and trial 6 settings to confirm whether depth 5 is genuinely the peak.
Thought: Depth 4 gave 0.5635. Testing depth 3 with the same configuration to see if even simpler trees further reduce overfitting on this imbalanced target.
Thought: Depth 4 is clearly optimal (peaking above depth 3 and 5). Now tuning n_estimators around 220 (testing 270) with lr=0.03.
Thought: Testing n_estimators=180 at depth 4 to check if early stopping occurs before 220.
Thought: Testing n_estimators=240 between 220 and 270.
Thought: Trial 13 reached 0.56425 with 240 trees. Now testing higher subsample (0.85 vs 0.75) to see if more row coverage helps.
Thought: subsample=0.85 dropped significantly. Testing subsample=0.70 to see if slightly more stochasticity improves PR-AUC beyond 0.75.
Thought: Subsample 0.75 is clearly optimal. Now evaluating colsample_bytree=0.70 (versus 0.80 in trial 13).
Thought: Testing colsample_bytree=0.85 with trial 13 settings to see if higher feature sampling improves on 0.80.
Thought: colsample 0.80 and subsample 0.75 are confirmed optimal. Now exploring L2 regularization: testing reg_lambda=1.0 (vs 0.5 in trial 13).
Thought: reg_lambda=1.0 decreased score from 0.56425. Testing smaller L2 regularization: reg_lambda=0.2.
Thought: reg_lambda=0.5 is optimal. Now testing L1 regularization: reg_alpha=0.01 (down from 0.05 in trial 13).
Thought: Testing reg_alpha=0.10 to check if stronger L1 sparsity improves generalization.
Thought: Testing slightly lower learning rate (0.025) with proportionally more estimators (290) to see if slower shrinkage finds a better minima.
Thought: Lower learning rate underperformed; testing slightly higher learning rate (0.035) with 210 estimators.
Thought: Testing n_estimators=250 at lr=0.03 to fine-tune tree count between 240 and 270.
Thought: 240 gave 0.56425 and 250 gave 0.56391. Testing n_estimators=235.
Thought: Testing subsample=0.78 (between 0.75 and 0.80) to fine-tune row subsampling.
Thought: 0.78 dropped significantly; testing subsample=0.73 just below 0.75.
Thought: Testing colsample_bytree=0.82 around 0.80.
Thought: Number of features sampled at 0.82 was identical due to rounding. Testing slight variation in L2 regularization: reg_lambda=0.6.
Thought: reg_lambda=0.6 dropped to 0.5622. Testing reg_lambda=0.4 for our final evaluation.
